params.name: S1.1
params.hypothesis: Right-hand stroke-edge detector: It reads the image through one 3x3 filter whose centre and right-hand weights are negative and whose left, top and bottom weights are positive, with a threshold that only dark ink clears. So it fires on a blank pixel that has dark ink on its left (and above and below it): the right-hand edge of a stroke, including the inside edge of a loop. Its average measures how much upright stroke edge the digit has, not how much ink: a thick stroke has no more right-hand edge than a thin one, and filling a loop removes the loop's inside edge. So an upright stroke should raise it more than the same stroke drawn horizontally, making the digit 30% taller should raise it more than making it 30% wider, and filling a digit's enclosed holes with ink should lower it, the opposite of what an ink meter would do. Self-probe: A 10-pixel upright stroke through the centre of the digit vs the same stroke horizontal: +0.66 SD against the control (95% interval +0.59 to +0.74, 1000 images; predicted up): agrees. The digit stretched 30% taller vs 30% wider: +1.22 SD against the control (95% interval +1.18 to +1.27, 1000 images; predicted up): agrees. The digit's enclosed holes filled with ink vs the digit unchanged (digits with holes): -0.73 SD against the control (95% interval -0.78 to -0.67, 379 images; predicted down): agrees. Behaviour (the conclusion): It fires on most 8s (92%), 0s (92%), 4s (84%), 6s (77%) and 9s (68%) and rarely on 1s (7%), 5s (11%), 7s (11%) and 3s (19%). Within each digit, the larger the amount of upright-stroke edge, the stronger the response (Spearman r = +0.41 averaged over digits; partial r = +0.36 with the digit and the ink count held fixed). Concept check: Named concepts that also hold within digits, with the ink held fixed: loop (more: fires on 87% of images with it vs 41% without, same digit); lower loop (more: fires on 91% of images with it vs 53% without, same digit); two loops (more: fires on 97% of images with it vs 85% without, same digit); waist (less: fires on 29% of images with it vs 46% without, same digit); 2 more in the table. The behaviour above is the reading; the concepts are a cross-check. Status: proven: every self-probe agrees (a directional one by at least 0.3 SD), and the reading holds within digits with the ink held fixed.

params.name: S1.2
params.hypothesis: Ink meter tilted to rising strokes: It reads the image through a 3x3 filter weighted along a line from lower left to upper right ('/'), minus S1.1's right-hand-edge map. Its average follows the amount of ink closely (Spearman r = 0.92 within digits), and beyond the ink it is higher for digits whose strokes lean right ('/') and lower where S1.1 finds solid right-hand edges. So thickening the strokes should raise it strongly, and leaning the whole digit to the right should raise it more than leaning it to the left by the same shear (the same ink either way). Self-probe: Thicken every stroke by one pixel (dilation) vs move the digit one pixel right: +1.09 SD against the control (95% interval +1.08 to +1.10, 1000 images; predicted up): agrees. The digit sheared to lean right vs to lean left (0.3 pixels per row): +0.35 SD against the control (95% interval +0.34 to +0.35, 1000 images; predicted up): agrees. Behaviour (the conclusion): It fires on most 0s (91%), 8s (77%), 6s (66%) and 2s (65%) and rarely on 1s (2%). Within each digit, the larger the amount of ink (ink pixels), the stronger the response (Spearman r = +0.92 averaged over digits; partial r = +0.93 with the digit held fixed). Concept check: Named concepts that also hold within digits, with the ink held fixed: a lot of ink (more: fires on 88% of images with it vs 18% without, same digit); tall stem (less: fires on 20% of images with it vs 60% without, same digit); wide (more: fires on 74% of images with it vs 38% without, same digit); slant (more: fires on 59% of images with it vs 42% without, same digit). The behaviour above is the reading; the concepts are a cross-check. Status: proven: every self-probe agrees (a directional one by at least 0.3 SD), and the reading holds within digits with the ink held fixed.

params.name: S1.3
params.hypothesis: Ink-amount meter: It reads the image through two filters (3x3, then 5x5 at half resolution) and its 14x14 map is a blurred copy of the ink: every dark pixel raises the map around it, whatever the stroke's direction or place. Its average is an ink meter (Spearman r = 0.986 with the ink count within digits). So thickening the strokes should raise it strongly, while a stroke of the same length should add about the same wherever it is placed and whichever way it runs, and stretching the digit taller or wider by the same factor should make no difference. Self-probe: Thicken every stroke by one pixel (dilation) vs move the digit one pixel right: +1.43 SD against the control (95% interval +1.41 to +1.44, 1000 images; predicted up): agrees. A 10-pixel horizontal stroke along the top of the digit vs the same stroke upright along its right edge: +0.03 SD against the control (95% interval +0.02 to +0.04, 1000 images; predicted no change): agrees. The digit stretched 30% taller vs 30% wider: -0.11 SD against the control (95% interval -0.11 to -0.10, 1000 images; predicted no change): agrees. Behaviour (the conclusion): It fires on most 0s (85%), 2s (73%), 8s (69%) and 3s (65%) and rarely on 1s (3%). Within each digit, the larger the amount of ink (ink pixels), the stronger the response (Spearman r = +0.99 averaged over digits; partial r = +0.99 with the digit held fixed). Concept check: Named concepts that also hold within digits, with the ink held fixed: a lot of ink (more: fires on 96% of images with it vs 8% without, same digit). The behaviour above is the reading; the concepts are a cross-check. Status: proven: every self-probe agrees (a directional one by at least 0.3 SD), and the reading holds within digits with the ink held fixed.

params.name: S1.4
params.hypothesis: Left-boundary detector (coarse): At a coarse 7x7 scale it reads S1.2's ink map with positive weights on the cells to the right and negative weights on the cells to the left. So it fires on empty cells that have ink just to their right: the left boundary of the digit (and of any stroke with space on its left), most strongly in the left half of the image and the lower rows. The longer the digit's left side and the more empty space to its left, the higher it is; ink placed to the left of the digit takes that space away. So an upright stroke drawn just right of the digit (a new left boundary with space before it) should raise it more than the same stroke drawn horizontally in the same place; the same upright stroke should raise it more right of the digit than left of it; and moving the digit 4 pixels right should raise it compared with moving it 4 pixels left. Self-probe: A 10-pixel stroke drawn 3 pixels right of the digit, upright vs horizontal: +0.57 SD against the control (95% interval +0.53 to +0.61, 1000 images; predicted up): agrees. A 10-pixel upright stroke drawn 3 pixels right of the digit vs 3 pixels left of it: +1.37 SD against the control (95% interval +1.29 to +1.44, 1000 images; predicted up): agrees. The digit moved 4 pixels right vs 4 pixels left: +1.90 SD against the control (95% interval +1.86 to +1.94, 1000 images; predicted up): agrees. Behaviour (the conclusion): It fires on most 8s (87%), 6s (85%), 0s (71%), 4s (67%) and 9s (61%) and rarely on 1s (2%), 7s (9%) and 5s (23%). Within each digit, the larger the number of image rows the digit spans (the length of its left side), the stronger the response (Spearman r = +0.28 averaged over digits; partial r = +0.38 with the digit and the ink count held fixed). Concept check: Named concepts that also hold within digits, with the ink held fixed: open left side (less: fires on 26% of images with it vs 44% without, same digit); waist (less: fires on 35% of images with it vs 48% without, same digit). The behaviour above is the reading; the concepts are a cross-check. Status: proven: every self-probe agrees (a directional one by at least 0.3 SD), and the reading holds within digits with the ink held fixed.

annotations.hypothesis: Diagonal strokes and the base: S8.1 ('/' strokes) reads the image and feeds S8.2 (the base stroke), S8.3 (lower '/' strokes) and S8.4 ('\' edges); S8.2 also feeds S8.3. S8.4 reads the image again with the opposite diagonal (and S8.1's path through an inner node). Every child except S8.1 feeds the scores directly. What the combination adds is both diagonals and the base: a '\' stroke instead of a '/' moves S8.4 by +0.85 SD and S8.1 by -0.41 SD, and a horizontal stroke along the bottom instead of the top moves S8.2 by +0.82 SD and S8.1 by -0.02 SD. A 10-class classifier on all four children's pooled exits reaches 82% (cross-validated), against 51% for the best child alone (S8.2). Self-probe: A '\' stroke through the centre vs the same stroke '/' (S8.4): +0.85 SD against the control (95% interval +0.80 to +0.91, 1000 images; predicted up): agrees. The same edit (S8.1): -0.41 SD against the control (95% interval -0.43 to -0.39, 1000 images; predicted down): agrees. A horizontal stroke along the bottom vs the top of the digit (S8.2): +0.82 SD against the control (95% interval +0.79 to +0.86, 1000 images; predicted up): agrees. The same edit (S8.1): -0.02 SD against the control (95% interval -0.03 to -0.01, 1000 images; predicted no change): agrees. The two diagonal detectors move in opposite directions under the same edit, and the base detector responds to where a horizontal stroke is while S8.1 does not. Behaviour (the conclusion): Its main exit (h90, from S8.3): it fires on most 0s (93%), 6s (91%) and 2s (88%) and rarely on 5s (14%) and 1s (17%). Concept check: Named concepts that also hold within digits, with the ink held fixed: filled (less: fires on 0% of images with it vs 22% without, same digit); tall stem (less: fires on 25% of images with it vs 61% without, same digit); wide (more: fires on 66% of images with it vs 39% without, same digit); slant (more: fires on 63% of images with it vs 36% without, same digit); 1 more in the table. The behaviour above is the reading; the concepts are a cross-check. Status: proven: every self-probe on the children agrees (a directional one by at least 0.3 SD).

superseded.hypothesis: 3-vs-8 separator (S8): Combines S8.1 (No-stem detector · with a closed lower loop (S8.1)), S8.2 (No-stem detector · with a closed lower loop (S8.2)), S8.3 (No-stem detector (S8.3)) and S8.4 (Lower-loop detector). S8.1 feeds S8.2, S8.3 and S8.4; S8.2 feeds S8.3. Together they separate 3s from 8s (95% balanced accuracy, cross-validated) much better than the best part alone (S8.4: 74%). Its strongest exit (map h90): it responds when the image lacks a tall vertical stem: it is held back by a long, near-vertical stroke running most of the digit's height. So it fires on 0s (93%), 6s (90%), 2s (88%) and 4s (56%), and on 1s that have no tall vertical stem (90% vs 5% without), and on 7s that have no tall vertical stem (55% vs 4% without). Evidence: Overall s = -0.56; within digits s = -0.55 on average over 7 digits; with the amount of ink held fixed, r = -0.18; add_stem edit: -0.15 SD against its control (too small to count). No image edit tested it (or the edit's effect was too small): supported, not proven.

annotations.name: root
annotations.title: Digit scores from the structures
annotations.hypothesis: Digit scores from the structures: The ten scores are exact sums: a constant plus one term per structure that feeds the score maps (and one for the image directly), each a kernel on the structure's exits, averaged over the map and mixed by the head (largest reconstruction error 2.1e-14). A digit can be recognised because a structure fires for it, or because a structure stays silent for it: the silence keeps a rival digit's score down. So waking a structure that a digit needs silent (drawing the stroke it detects) should lower that digit's score margin more than drawing the same stroke where the structure does not see it. Self-probe: On the probe images the same structure comes first for 9 of the 10 digits. On 4s, a 10-pixel horizontal stroke along the top of the digit vs the same stroke upright there (the '4' score margin): -5.58 SD against the control (95% interval -5.89 to -5.29, 97 images; predicted down): agrees. On 6s, a 10-pixel horizontal stroke along the top of the digit vs the same stroke upright there (the '6' score margin): -1.63 SD against the control (95% interval -2.41 to -0.85, 99 images; predicted down): agrees. On 1s, a 10-pixel '\' stroke through the centre vs the same stroke upright, along the 1 (the '1' score margin; wakes S8.4): -6.39 SD against the control (95% interval -6.72 to -6.06, 113 images; predicted down): agrees. On 1s, a 10-pixel horizontal stroke along the bottom of the digit vs the same stroke upright there (the '1' score margin; wakes S8.2): +2.98 SD against the control (95% interval +2.70 to +3.27, 113 images; predicted down): contradicts. On 7s, a 10-pixel horizontal stroke along the bottom of the digit vs the same stroke upright there (the '7' score margin; wakes S8.2): -0.29 SD against the control (95% interval -0.57 to +0.02, 104 images; predicted down): too small. Behaviour (the conclusion): Which structure each digit depends on most (discovery images): 0s on S8 (Diagonal strokes and the base), which fires on 93% of them (holding its term at the average costs 60% of 0s, most of them to '8'); 1s on S8 (Diagonal strokes and the base), which is silent (below its median response) on 83% of them (holding its term at the average costs 99% of 1s, most of them to '6'); 2s on S7 (Low-right horizontal-stroke detector), which fires on 98% of them (holding its term at the average costs 9% of 2s, most of them to '3'); 3s on S8 (Diagonal strokes and the base), which is silent (below its median response) on 74% of them (holding its term at the average costs 8% of 3s, most of them to '9'); 4s on S5 (Top-bar detector), which is silent (below its median response) on 100% of them (holding its term at the average costs 90% of 4s, most of them to '9'); 5s on S4 (Upright-left-side detector), which fires on 99% of them (holding its term at the average costs 24% of 5s, most of them to '3'); 6s on S5 (Top-bar detector), which is silent (below its median response) on 99% of them (holding its term at the average costs 79% of 6s, most of them to '0'); 7s on S8 (Diagonal strokes and the base), which is silent (below its median response) on 57% of them (holding its term at the average costs 74% of 7s, most of them to '2'); 8s on S8 (Diagonal strokes and the base), which is silent (below its median response) on 57% of them (holding its term at the average costs 18% of 8s, most of them to '9'); 9s on S8 (Diagonal strokes and the base), which is silent (below its median response) on 69% of them (holding its term at the average costs 9% of 9s, most of them to '0'). So digits are recognised by a structure that fires: 0s by S8; 2s by S7; 5s by S4 and by a structure that stays silent: 1s, 3s, 7s, 8s and 9s need S8 silent; 4s and 6s need S5 silent. Status: contested: an image edit went against the prediction.

words.top_bar: a horizontal bar along the top
words.open_upper_left: an upper curve open to the left
words.open_upper_right: an upper curve open to the right
words.open_lower_left: a lower curve open to the left
words.two_left_openings: two curves open to the left, one above the other
words.ends_3plus: three or more free stroke ends
words.waist: a narrow central crossing (the waist of an 8)
words.left_heavy: more ink on the left half than the right
words.wide: a wide digit (box at least 0.8 as wide as tall)
words.low_ink_centre: ink concentrated in the lower half

rules.loop: enclosed background, paper fully surrounded by ink
rules.two_loops: digits with two separate enclosed regions
rules.upper_loop: an enclosed region in the upper half of the digit
rules.lower_loop: an enclosed region in the lower half of the digit
rules.stem: a long, near-vertical stroke running most of the digit's height
rules.top_bar: a horizontal stroke across the top of the digit
rules.open_left: a digit whose left side is open in the middle rows (as in 3, 7 and many 2s and 1s)
rules.open_upper_left: an upper curve that opens to the left, ink above, below and to its right (the top of a 2, 3 or 7)
rules.open_upper_right: an upper curve that opens to the right (the top of a 5 or 6)
rules.open_lower_left: a lower curve that opens to the left (the bottom of a 3, 5 or 9)
rules.two_left_openings: two curves opening to the left, one above the other (the shape of a 3)
rules.open_top: a gap that opens upwards between two strokes (the top of a 4)
rules.junction: points where three or more strokes meet
rules.diagonal: strokes that run diagonally rather than straight up or across
rules.heavy_ink: the amount of ink in the image
rules.waist: an inked row in the 40-60 % band whose ink is at most 40 % of the box width, centred between 30 % and 60 % of it
rules.left_heavy: the left half of the ink's bounding box holds more ink than the right half
rules.one_piece: ink that forms one connected stroke (8-connected, pieces of at least 3 pixels)
rules.coherent: ink that forms one coherent shape (at least 90% of the ink in its largest piece)
rules.filled: ink that fills its bounding box (at least 60% of the box), as a blob does
rules.wide: the ink's bounding box is at least 0.8 times as wide as it is tall
rules.slanted: the principal axis of the ink pixels leans right by more than 15 degrees from vertical
rules.low_ink_centre: the ink's centre of mass is below the box centre by more than 5 % of the box height
